source_snapshot.procedure: Enable DDNS in WebUI, use a DHCP-provided domain, require an error when domain service is unreachable, then select and enter a custom domain.
source_snapshot.criteria: Correct DDNS display and domain resolution after the DHCP-domain Apply step.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; runs public-recursive nslookup and reads LAN data but does not prove a BMC-originated dynamic update.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION for provider, domains, negative path, authoritative records and cleanup.

old_problem: The case stayed Pending despite a coherent positive/negative/custom branch model; the missing DHCP/DDNS provider values, credentials, expected records and custom acceptance are normal Project inputs.
disposition_reason: RFC-defined DHCP FQDN and DNS UPDATE behavior supplies the technical model, while the project owns its zone and policy. The review preserves the successful DHCP-domain path, the explicit unreachable-provider error path and the custom-domain path independently. It does not treat recursive lookup alone as proof of a BMC update.
decision_basis: Direct review covered XLSX row 829, its DeepSeek columns, exact GPT V2 object and historical record.
RFC 4702 defines DHCPv4 Client FQDN negotiation and leaves update authority to site policy; RFC 2136 defines DNS UPDATE transactions.
The source explicitly describes a negative UI oracle when the domain server cannot be contacted; that visual state must be retained.
The custom-domain branch lacks concrete values but has an identifiable action and can be completed by a project-owned zone/record contract under ED-36.

test_case.test_name: Verify BMC DDNS DHCP-domain, failure-message and custom-domain paths
test_case.purpose: Verify readable DDNS WebUI behavior and authoritative dynamic registration for the DHCP-provided domain, verify an explicit error when the approved provider is intentionally unavailable, then save and, when supported, register an approved custom domain without stale-record or credential leakage.
required_package: Isolated authoritative DNS/DDNS zone, update policy/credentials, resolver, TTL and server logs
DHCP scope/lease carrying the approved domain/FQDN policy and expected BMC address/record ownership
Approved custom FQDN and expected A/AAAA/PTR records plus collision/cleanup policy
BMC DDNS capability/UI fields, protected credentials, prior state and restore sequence
Controlled provider-unreachable method that affects only the test path and exact expected UI error text/state
test_case.test_command: Back up DDNS/DNS/DHCP state and clear only test-zone records per policy. Phase A: in the actual WebUI enable DDNS, choose the DHCP-provided domain, Apply, then correlate DHCP lease/FQDN option, BMC audit, authoritative update log and fresh authoritative A/AAAA/PTR queries; capture readable UI status. Phase B: make only the approved test provider path unreachable, Apply once, and verify the explicit unable-to-pull-domain state with no false success; restore provider access without automatic retry. Phase C: select custom domain, enter the approved FQDN, Apply under the Project contract, and verify saved UI plus authoritative update/record if supported. Remove test records and restore prior settings.
test_case.expected_result: DHCP mode displays the negotiated domain and creates/updates exactly the approved authoritative record set for the BMC within the deadline. The isolated failure phase reports the specified visible error and does not claim resolution. Custom mode saves the exact approved name and produces the project-defined authoritative result without overwriting another owner. Cleanup removes or restores only test-owned records and BMC settings.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires actual WebUI evidence, provider/DHCP logs and fresh authoritative queries tied to the exact BMC for each applicable branch. A cached public-recursive answer or `lan print` cannot prove DDNS. FAIL includes absent/wrong/stale records, wrong owner/address, missing failure message, false success, custom value loss, unauthorized update, secret exposure or cleanup failure. Missing zone/domain/package makes execution NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Use only an isolated project-owned update zone; never test against public DNS or 8.8.8.8 as authority
Protect update/BMC credentials and redact UI/log evidence
Use unique names and pre-check ownership to prevent overwriting unrelated records
Limit the negative-path outage to the test provider route and do not auto-retry after unexpected behavior
Back up and restore DHCP/DDNS settings and remove only test-owned records
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware identity and before/after DDNS WebUI screenshots
DHCP lease/FQDN option and chosen update-responsibility policy
Authoritative server update/audit logs and fresh uncached record queries with TTL
Controlled outage proof and exact visible error state
Custom-domain Apply, saved value and authoritative result or documented supported-scope expectation
Record/configuration cleanup and final BMC/DNS health
test_case.recovery: Restore provider reachability and the saved BMC DDNS/DNS/DHCP settings through the approved path. Revert or delete only records created for this case using the authoritative change log. Preserve any collision/false update evidence and stop before retrying or changing another record.

source_conflict.reason: Positive, negative and custom-domain source paths are compatible; custom expected values are Project Configuration.

blocked.reason: The DDNS operations and oracles are defined; provider/domain/security data are supplyable readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: DHCP FQDN policy, authoritative zone/update credentials, expected records/TTL, negative-path error, custom FQDN and cleanup.
